summary:
Alfred “Lord” Hayes (1928–2005) was an English wrestler, manager and commentator best known for his World Wrestling Federation work from 1982 to 1995. A judo black belt trained by Sir Atholl Oakeley, he wrestled in Britain and France from the late 1950s, using the name Judo Al Hayes and later performing as the White Angel. He held the Southern Area Heavyweight Championship and became a Conservative councillor in Islington.

After moving to North America, Hayes wrestled and managed in several promotions, adopting an aristocratic heel persona. His final match was in 1983. In the WWF, he worked as a road agent, interviewer, host and commentator, appearing on shows including Tuesday Night Titans and Prime Time Wrestling. His measured Oxford accent and distinctive laugh became familiar to viewers.

Hayes retired in 1995 after pay cuts and a serious car accident that led to the amputation of part of a leg. He died in Texas in 2005, aged 76. He was inducted into the WWE Hall of Fame’s Legacy Wing in 2018 and the Professional Wrestling Hall of Fame in 2014.
